The Knowledge Harvester — where packs come from

The SATOM team's separate tool that measures lab appliances and reads the vendor documentation, gates every change, and publishes the result as signed API and knowledge packs — the only source of vendor knowledge since SATOM 3.0.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereNot part of SATOM. Its output: Software Update → Knowledge packs / API library packs (URL /self-update/)
On this page
  • What is it?
  • What a pack carries
  • Where the knowledge comes from
  • From snapshot to your node
  • Do I need the harvester?
  • Troubleshooting
  • "this is a harvester TRANSPORT pack (lane 'harvester') …"
  • Items stay "local"
  • Release notes are missing for a build

What is it?#

The SATOM Knowledge Harvester is a separate tool, run by the SATOM team, that collects what Fortinet products expose about their configuration API and turns it into signed packs your SATOM imports. Nothing in SATOM calls it, it never talks to your node, and you do not install it: you receive its packs.

Since SATOM 3.0 it is the only source of vendor knowledge. SATOM itself no longer reads any vendor web site.

What a pack carries#

Both lanes carry the same sections, and every pack is a full snapshot, never a delta:

Section Content
library per exact build: the CLI schema (tree), the field names show full-configuration prints, REST field names and types, vendor schemas, CLI reference tables and the public Ansible collections
docs the vendor release notes of FortiWeb, FortiADC, FortiAuthenticator, FortiAnalyzer and FortiGate; field catalogs per firmware line
cli-coverage the configuration blocks that exist only in the CLI, per version (names only)
factory the FortiWeb predefined Web Protection Profiles per build
field-map field rename candidates between builds — shown, never applied
baselines measured endpoint baselines per build, as reference
signature-meta public FortiGuard signature metadata — ships empty (see below)

What a pack never carries: configuration values (field names and types only; defaults only from vendor schemas or freshly created lab rows), device identity (lab devices become stable pseudonyms; serials, addresses and hostnames are never recorded) and signatures (each appliance downloads its own from FortiGuard).

ℹ️Note — Signature metadata ships empty

The harvester checks the FortiGuard site's terms before reading anything there. They do not permit collecting and redistributing that data, so the FortiGuard enrichment is disabled and the signature-meta section stays empty until it is permitted. Signature ids are shown without the extra metadata until then.

Where the knowledge comes from#

Source What it adds
Lab appliances FortiWeb 7.6.8 and 8.0.6, FortiGate 8.0.1, FortiAuthenticator 8.0.3: CLI schema, field names, REST sweeps and schemas, factory profiles, lab defaults
Vendor documentation release notes of every product, CLI reference tables
Public Ansible collections fortinet.fortios and fortinet.fortianalyzer
Earlier signed packs builds no lab appliance can re-measure today (for example FortiADC 8.0.3, FortiWeb 8.0.5), marked as archived and superseded as soon as an appliance measures that build

The harvester's SSH sessions send only read commands (get system status, tree, show …) and its REST calls are GETs.

From snapshot to your node#

  1. 1Snapshotevery section built in one run, with a date-free content fingerprint
  2. 2Content gateadditions approved automatically; any removal or change held for a maintainer's audited approval
  3. 3Sign per laneknowledge key for the rolling pack, API-pack key at each release
  4. 4Testimported into a staging SATOM; only a clean import is published
  5. 5Publishknowledge release + latest.json feed; API pack inside the release
Lane Name Published Reaches your node
API pack satom-apipack-<SATOM version> at every SATOM release; a parity gate refuses the release if anything the previous API pack carried is missing inside the update, imported by the update on the primary
Knowledge pack satom-apipack-kb-YYYYMMDD[.N] whenever the approved knowledge changes the knowledge feed (knowledge_fetch) or an upload — see Knowledge packs

Between packs, the newer snapshot wins whatever its lane, so a knowledge pack corrects the release's API pack without waiting for the next release. What your node measured or wrote itself always wins over both.

Do I need the harvester?#

No. Customers only import its packs. The keys and fingerprints that verify them are on Pack trust.

Troubleshooting#

"this is a harvester TRANSPORT pack (lane 'harvester') …"#

You were given the harvester's internal transport file. Import the API pack or knowledge pack published from it.

Items stay "local"#

Expected: your node measured that build itself, and local measurement wins.

Release notes are missing for a build#

Import the newest knowledge pack (Knowledge packs), then click Reload corpus in the Release notes window.

#knowledge harvester#satom-harvester#knowledge pack#api pack#lane#snapshot#content gate#lab#cli schema#release notes#fortiguard#signature metadata#crawler
